cells.tense: The read arrives whole and early right now, and you can leave what isn't yours to carry.
cells.act: build the smallest structure that holds it
cells.ask: Give a growing thing at home — a child, a plant, a project — a fixed hour or spot this week, then leave the arrangement to work while you step back.
cells.core:
You sense what needs tending before you could argue for it, and you don't force an answer out of the not-yet. Something in your care is coming along at its own speed, and your feel for what it needs keeps holding up. A little plain structure around it pairs well with that — containers, not control.

Choose an hour, a spot, a repeat, and build the smallest one that fits. Then step back from watching it so closely. If your read on it turns out wrong, the arrangement is still there and still useful, and you'll see the mismatch sooner for having stood back from it.
cells.sheetLine: You sense what to attend to, and can let it grow.
cells.verb: sensing what deserves care before you can argue for it

cells.tense: Pretty soon every unknown will need pinning down first, and the gathering becomes a wall.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Set down what you've been researching about something you're growing, name what growing well would honestly look like, and take a step toward it this week.
cells.core:
Before long every unknown has to be cornered first, and the pile of angles you're holding becomes a wall between you and the thing itself. That isn't insight talking — it's insight running hot, demanding the whole route before you move. What's growing goes unwatered while you guard the collection. The container you were building around it turns into a cage.

Step toward what you actually want. Write it plainly, in your own words: what growing well would honestly look like here, not the version that sounds credible. Then do the smallest real thing in that direction. Not knowing the rest yet is allowed. What you want is itself information, and it's been sitting under the pile.
cells.sheetLine: Demand the whole route and nothing gets to grow.
cells.verb: sensing what deserves care before you can argue for it
cells.place: beside something growing, at its own pace

cells.tense: Your own read has gone quiet here, and you hand it to others to hold before you believe it.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Do the next right thing in something you're tending that has no clear answer — the one you can see from here, not the full route.
cells.core:
The fog isn't in what you're growing — it's that a certainty keeps being waited for in a form it doesn't arrive in. What you sense quietly keeps proving right, and your name keeps being left off it. The confusion lives in the reading of it, not in the thing itself. Attention has nowhere clear to rest.

Move on one step of light. Take something in your care with no clear answer and do the next right thing within it, the one visible from right here. A route tends to show itself in pieces, and none of them is required to be the whole of it. Let the piece you can see be enough.

cells.tense: Your calls keep turning out well and keep surprising you, and no one has signed for them.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: Trace a recent choice you'd call luck back to the moment you actually knew, say it was yours — then settle a single thing owed in either direction, once.
cells.core:
Your calls keep coming out right and keep taking you by surprise, as though someone else did the deciding. Luck gets the credit, or timing, or another person — anything but whoever read the room before it said anything. The work keeps happening and the name keeps being left off it. Balance sits unadjusted too.

Find the read inside one choice you'd call random, the moment you knew. Say to yourself first that it was yours. Then settle a single thing in either direction — something owed, something due you — one exchange, no tally kept. Balance returns by adjustment, not by scoring, and what steers you gets usable on purpose once it's yours.

attempts.check: The record supports that perceptions land accurately and that the person tends what's growing, but nothing supports my draft line that those around them have come to lean on the knowing itself — I invented that dependence; the reader could fairly say the knowing is mostly private. The ask survives a wrong read: naming what's unformed and leaving it be teaches something the person can keep even if my picture of their situation misses, though the 'no urgency to resolve' clause is the part most likely to be off. The sentence that serves me more than them is the sheetLine about being trusted to sense things rightly — it flatters the seat, and I cut it back.
